Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 7:26am

Kai Lohmann kicked five vital goals as Brisbane earned a vital win over Geelong at Kardinia Park to break into the top four.

  (Getty Images: AFL Photos/Michael Willson)

AFL premiers Brisbane resisted a remarkable Geelong fightback in a see-sawing battle to surge into the top four with a 22-point statement win over their great modern rivals.

The Lions kicked the first eight goals of the game but saw a 43-point lead slashed to just one before steadying in a 19.9 (123) to 14.17 (101) victory at Kardinia Park on Thursday night.

It improves Brisbane's record to 10-6 as they leapfrog the Cats (9-7) into fourth spot on the ladder.

The Lions, who were belted by Geelong to the tune of 41 points on home turf in May, have won four straight matches since their mid-season stumble and kicked triple-figure scores in each of them.

Will Ashcroft (32 disposals) and Lachie Neale (28) were key in their latest triumph, as was Brisbane's efficiency in attack, where Kai Lohmann kicked five goals.

Geelong dominated the inside-50 count (69-52) but coughed up goals from almost 50 per cent of the Lions' forward entries in the first three quarters.

Young key forward Logan Morris and the brilliant Zac Bailey (20 disposals) kicked three goals apiece.

"We were probably a little bit fortunate that we kicked really straight and they didn't, but our efficiency going inside-50 was exceptionally good," Lions coach Chris Fagan said.

"To come here and win at this oval is a tough thing to do. It's almost worth eight points when you win here, I think.

"The fact that the boys were able to do that and stay mentally strong throughout the game when they were challenged was a real pleasing aspect of tonight."

Connor McKenna (two goals) did well as a defensive forward on Cats star Tom Stewart, Darcy Wilmot (26 touches) shone in defence, and Darcy Gardiner blanketed Jeremy Cameron (four disposals) before hobbling off late with a hamstring injury.

Geelong captain Patrick Dangerfield (five goals) was outstanding for the home side, Bailey Smith (31 disposals) and Max Holmes (30) were major ball-winners, and Ollie Dempsey (two goals, 22 disposals) was busy on a wing.

Charlie Cameron sparked the Lions's hot start with two goals in the opening two minutes and the visitors piled on eight straight in a stunning early burst.

Brisbane shredded their opponents on turnover, with their first seven inside-50 entries resulting in majors.

Geelong eventually managed a response through Dangerfield moments before quarter-time and the skipper kicked another brilliant goal soon after the break.

Lions gun Lachie Neale copped an accidental knee from teammate Cam Rayner (24 disposals, one goal) and stumbled as he tried to get up. He was sent off the field for a concussion test, which he passed, and was heckled by a Cats fan on his way to the change room.

It came as Geelong added 6.6 to 1.6 in the second term, including three goals from Shannon Neale, to slash the margin to seven points by half-time.

Despite another two majors from Dangerfield, the Lions flexed their collective muscle again with eight goals to four in the third quarter.

They turned for home 30 points in front and kept the Cats at arm's length in the final term.

"They really took their chances. Their kicking for goal was really good and ours was poor," Geelong coach Chris Scott said.

"It was a strange game in that probably for more than 50 per cent of the game we were in control of it, and either couldn't take our chances when we generated them or allowed them back into it with some basic errors."

Meanwhile, Scott backed Cameron to fight his way through a "flat spot" amid a spotlight on the out-of-sorts star's form and fitness.

The 33-year-old flew for some marks one-handed and managed just four disposals while going goalless for the third time this season.

Scott said Geelong's coaching staff are asking questions of Cameron and club doctors.

"The feedback we're getting is he's well and truly good enough to play," Scott said.

"I think you can take it as read that we do not play players that we don't think can perform."

Scott likened Cameron's situation to that of Geelong captain Patrick Dangerfield, who has had to build his way into the season after an interrupted start.

"We tend to give our champions maybe a little bit more room than some others and we're confident that he'll find his way through it," Scott said.

"If he (Cameron) can't in the short term then we'll have a think about how we can help him through it even more.

"It's a strange situation for us to be talking about given how good he's been for us."

Look back at how all the action unfolded in our live blog.

Thu 2 Jul 2026 at 11:19pm

By Andrew McGarry

So that wraps things up for the first game of round 17, and a very entertaining and occasionally puzzling game it was too.

There will be some injuries to keep an eye on over the weekend, with Max Holmes' hamstring on a watch, along with Darcy Gardiner's hamstring which looks a bit more serious.

Zac Bailey looked a little proppy near the end of the game, and his hamstring might bear a little watching too.

Bravo to Brisbane for winning a second straight game at Kardinia Park, as you can see from the ladder below, this puts them back into the top four although the Crows could change this if they win against West Coast tomorrow night.

Speaking of that, we will be back tomorrow evening for a Friday night double-header (or overlapper). It starts with a cracker at the SCG between the Sydney Swans and the Western Bulldogs, followed a little later by West Coast vs Adelaide.

You can join us for those ones tomorrow, but in the meantime this is Andrew McGarry, thanking you for joining us tonight and wishing you all a very good night.

Thu 2 Jul 2026 at 11:09pm

By Andrew McGarry

Geelong coach Chris Scott looks a lot calmer than he was during the game when he pulled a phone line out of the wall.

He puts the high-scoring game to "a good opposition".

He called it "a really strange game".

"To concede eight goals early in a game ... we fed their game way too much.

"If you give them (Brisbane) goals, they're going to kick some goals anyway.

"If you do that, they're going to be hard to stop."

He praised the Lions for really taking their chances, but said "for more than 50 per cent of the game we were in control, but we didn't take our chances or allowed them back in the game with basic errors."

Thu 2 Jul 2026 at 10:46pm

By Andrew McGarry

Brisbane skipper Harris Andrews has spoken to Channel Seven after his team's crucial win over Geelong.

"I think we were eight, nine points up at half-time (even after Geelong's big second quarter) - if you'd told us before the game we'd have that lead (at half-time) I think we would have taken that," he said.

"And we were able to go ahead from there (and win)."

Andrews said as a defender, he was a "glass half-empty guy", who "didn't look beyond training next Tuesday".

Asked about the Lions' position going into the final stretch of the season, he said:

"It's an ongoing process. One thing I think we can hang our hats on the last couple of years, when the challenge comes we stand up."

Key Event

Thu 2 Jul 2026 at 10:27pm

By Andrew McGarry

Patrick Dangerfield had a huge game for Geelong, with five vital goals to keep his team in the game.

But the skipper is clearly frustrated with the loss, and he's spoken to Channel Seven about the start to the game.

"I think that's (the first quarter) the game, isn't it?" he said.

"There was also a patch in the third quarter where we didn't take our opportunities and they (the Lions) as a premiership team, they took theirs."

Thu 2 Jul 2026 at 10:17pm

By Andrew McGarry

The noise dies down in the final minute, as Geelong fans realise it isn't going to happen.

Darcy Fort takes a late mark, and he slots the goal.

The siren sounds, and it's Brisbane who take the points in a high-scoring epic!

A huge win, it's their second straight victory at Kardinia Park.

If that isn't a signal to everyone that the defending premiers are back, I don't know what is.

They will want to improve on giving away strings of goals at bad times, but make no mistake - this is an important win.

Thu 2 Jul 2026 at 10:14pm

By Andrew McGarry

A key mark at half-back led to Brisbane hoofing it forward.

They have it in their forward half with under two minutes to go, and Geelong needs three goals.

Thu 2 Jul 2026 at 10:12pm

By Andrew McGarry

The clock has ticked down with Brisbane trying to stop Geelong marks and run things.

But a desperate kick clears for the Cats, and 10-15 seconds later the ball is in Ollie Dempsey's hands in the pocket.

He kicks it! 16 points, 2:46 left. Can Geelong do it? Can Brisbane hang on?

Thu 2 Jul 2026 at 10:09pm

By Andrew McGarry

It's not over yet!

The Cats go forward and it's the skipper again!

Patrick Dangerfield hoiks a kick home from distance, and it's 22 points with five minutes on the clock.

Thu 2 Jul 2026 at 10:08pm

By Andrew McGarry

Time is definitely running out for Geelong, and that was not what they needed. A kick from Connor O'Sullivan missed.

The lead is 28 points with just over six minutes on the clock.

If Geelong has an answer they have to find it now.

Thu 2 Jul 2026 at 10:06pm

By Andrew McGarry

The Cats are still coming, but they can't find the target.

Tanner Bruhn laced the ball inside 50, but Ryan Lester produced a great leap and mark to stop the attack.

Thu 2 Jul 2026 at 10:04pm

By Andrew McGarry

Time is ticking, and the Lions are trying desperately to hold the ball inside Geelong's half.

A big kick from Cam Rayner hits hands and comes to Kai Lohmann, who snaps perfectly and the crowd goes quiet!

That's five for Kai, and the lead is 29 points!

Advantage Brisbane!

Thu 2 Jul 2026 at 10:01pm

By Andrew McGarry

We have just over 10 minutes on the countdown clock, and that could be a big moment.

Darcy Gardiner, who has been immense in the Brisbane backline, is limping off the ground with a possibly calf or hamstring issue.

Thu 2 Jul 2026 at 9:59pm

By Andrew McGarry

The chances are going at both ends, and Jarrod Berry has taken a mark inside 50.

He has the set shot from in front, this is a big chance - but he misses to the right!

Still 23 points, four goals would win it for Geelong.

Thu 2 Jul 2026 at 9:57pm

By Andrew McGarry

The pressure is rising steadily (if it wasn't already high) and Geelong go inside 50, and Shaun Mannagh has a snap from 30m out.

It curls, but too late and goes just to the right.

The lead is 22 points with 13 minutes on the clock.

Thu 2 Jul 2026 at 9:55pm

By Andrew McGarry

That was a crazy few minutes, with the ball pinging from one end to another, with desperate tackles and risky passes and no one quite able to finish off movements.

Finally Geelong got the ball inside 50, it came off hands and fell to Ollie Wiltshire who ran on and snapped on the run, but it went just wide.

23 points the margin.

Thu 2 Jul 2026 at 9:49pm

By Andrew McGarry

It's been a frenetic start to the final term, but it's Geelong who get the vital early goal - to Oisin Mullin!

The lead is back to 24 points, and there is PLENTY of time.

Thu 2 Jul 2026 at 9:47pm

By Andrew McGarry

Geelong midfielder Max Holmes has been off for a fair period of the third term with an apparent hamstring issue.

He's back out there again for the final term. Will he last?
